ec:2003:q19.title: GATE EC 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 19
ec:2003:q19.question: Without any additional circuitry, an 8:1 MUX can be used to obtain
options: some but not all Boolean functions of 3 variables
all functions of 3 variables but none of 4 variables
all functions of 3 variables and some but not all of 4 variables

detailed_solution.concept: Digital Circuits - Multiplexer Realization of Boolean Functions
detailed_solution.markdown:
### 1. Problem Formulation
We are asked what functions can be implemented using an **8:1 Multiplexer (MUX)** **without any additional circuitry** (i.e. using only the multiplexer, tie-offs to logic $0$ and logic $1$, and true variable inputs, with no external inverters or logic gates).

---

### 2. Functional Capacity of an 8:1 MUX

An $8:1$ MUX has:
- $n = 3$ select lines ($S_2, S_1, S_0$)
- $2^n = 8$ data inputs ($I_0, I_1, \dots, I_7$)

#### Case 1: 3-Variable Functions $f(A, B, C)$
- Connect the 3 variables $A, B, C$ directly to the select lines $S_2, S_1, S_0$.
- Each of the 8 minterms corresponds uniquely to one data input $I_k$ ($k \in \{0, 1, \dots, 7\}$).
- By tying each data input line $I_k$ directly to either constant **logic 1** ($V_{CC}$) or constant **logic 0** (GND), **every possible Boolean function of 3 variables** ($2^{2^3} = 256$ functions) can be implemented.
- No external gates or inverters are needed.
- **Result:** **All functions of 3 variables can be implemented.**

#### Case 2: 4-Variable Functions $f(A, B, C, D)$
- Connect 3 of the variables (say $A, B, C$) to the select lines $S_2, S_1, S_0$.
- For each combination of $(A, B, C)$, the function value depends on the fourth variable $D$.
- Thus, each data input $I_k$ must be set to one of four possibilities:
  1. $0$ (constant low, GND)
  2. $1$ (constant high, $V_{CC}$)
  3. $D$ (direct variable connection)
  4. $\bar{D}$ (complemented variable)
- Connecting $0, 1$, or $D$ requires **no additional circuitry**.
- However, generating the complemented literal $\bar{D}$ requires an **inverter (NOT gate)**, which constitutes additional external circuitry.
- Therefore, only those 4-variable functions whose Shannon expansion terms do not require $\bar{D}$ on any data line can be implemented without an external inverter.
- **Result:** **Some but not all functions of 4 variables can be implemented.**

---

### 3. Conclusion & Option Matching
- Without additional circuitry, an 8:1 MUX can implement **all functions of 3 variables and some but not all of 4 variables**.
- This directly matches **Option C**.

**Correct Answer: Option C**

$$\begin{bmatrix} \dot{X_1}\\\dot{X_2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &0 \\ 1& 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} X_1\\X_2 \end{bmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{bmatrix} X_1(0)\\X_2(0) \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\0 \end{bmatrix}$$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} (s I-A) &=\left[\begin{array}{ll} s & 0 \\ 0 & s \end{array}\right]-\left[\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{array}\right] \\ &=\left[\begin{array}{cc} s-1 & 0 \\ -1 & s-1 \end{array}\right] \\ (s I-A)^{-1} &=\frac{\left[\begin{array}{cc} (s-1) & 0 \\ +1 & (s-1) \end{array}\right]}{(s-1)^{2}}\\ &=\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{1}{s-1} & 0 \\ \frac{+1}{(s-1)^{2}} & \frac{1}{s-1}\end{array}\right] \\ L^{-1}[s I-A]^{-1}&=e^{A t}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}e^{t} & 0 \\ t e^{t} & e^{t}\end{array}\right] \\ &=\left[\begin{array}{cc}e^{t} & 0 \\ t e^{t} & e^{t}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c}e^{t} \\ t e^{t}\end{array}\right] \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ec:2003:q74.title: GATE EC 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 74
ec:2003:q74.question:
A DSB-SC signal is to be generated with a carrier frequency $f_{c}$ = 1 MHz using anon-linear device with the input-output characteristic
$V_{0}=a_{0}v_{i}+a_{1}v_{i}^{3}$
where $a_{0}$ and $a_{1}$ are constants. The output of the non-linear device can be filtered by an appropriate band pass filter.
Let $V_{i}=A_{c}^{'}\cos (2\pi f_{c}'t)+m(t)$, where m(t) is the message signal. Then the value of $f_{c}^{'}$ (in MHz) is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} V_{0}=a_{0} v_{i}+a_{1} v_{i}^{3}\\ =a_{0}\left(A_{c}^{i} \cos \omega_{c}^{i} t\right)+a_{d} m(t)+a_{1} A_{c}^{3} \cos ^{3}\left(n_{c}^{i} t\right. \\ +a_{1} m^{3}(t)+3 a_{3} m^{2}(t) A_{c}^{i} \cos \omega_{c}^{i} t \\ +3 a_{1} A_{c}^{\prime} \cos ^{2} \omega_{c}^{i} t m(t) \end{array}$$

For DSB-SC, we are concerned with only last term.

$$\begin{aligned} m(t) \cos \omega_{c} t \rightarrow f_{c} &=1 \mathrm{MHz} \\ \text { For } \cos ^{2} \text { term, } 2 \omega_{c}^{i} &=2 \pi \times 1 \mathrm{MHz} \\ \cos ^{2} \text { term, } 2 \omega_{c}^{i} &=2 \pi \times 1 \mathrm{MHz} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ec:2003:q84.title: GATE EC 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 84
ec:2003:q84.question: Medium 1 has the electrical permittivity $\varepsilon _{1}=1.5\varepsilon _{0}$ farad/m and occupies the region to the left of x = 0 plane. Medium 2 has the electrical permittivity $\varepsilon _{2}=2.5\varepsilon _{0}$ farad/m and occupies the region to the right of x = 0 plane. If $E_{1}$ in medium 1 is $E_{1}$ = $(2u_{x}-3u_{y}+1u_{z})$ volt/m, then  $E_{2}$ in medium 2 is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \vec{E}_{1} &=2 u_{x}-3 u_{y}+1 u_{z} \\ \vec{E}_{1 t} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}=E_{2 t} &(x=0 \text { plane}) \\ \vec{E}_{1 n} &=2 u_{x} \\ \vec{D}_{1 n} &=\vec{D}_{2 n}=\epsilon \vec{E} \\ \Rightarrow \epsilon_{1} \vec{E}_{1 n} &=\epsilon_{2} \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ &=1.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot 2 u_{x}=2.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2 n} &=\frac{3}{2.5} u_{x}=1.2 u_{x} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=\vec{E}_{2 t}+\vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}+1.2 u_{x} \\ &=1.2u_{x}-3.0u_{y}+1.0u_{z} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.
